findings.impact: An implementation can replace accepted test content without detection.
findings.text: The proposed blocked-record path carry does not retain an accepted checkpoint or change preserve_check, which returns when the producer is blocked. Per-commit scans cover only origin..head; an already-published protected change can avoid that scan and the final-tree check. Require final-tree comparison using a verified accepted checkpoint, or refuse preserved submissions while blocked, and test the already-published work-tip case with blocked_findings disabled. Impact: an implementation can replace accepted tests without detection. Material: true.

output.summary: Blocked-producer submissions are refused and attempt provenance is retained for safe retry.
Approved the reviewed design for preserving accepted tests across blocked retries and recovering affected goals.

responses.adversary_design:1:1: fixed: Refuse all preserved consumer checkpoint submissions while the producer is blocked, independently of blocked_findings; test the previously published work-tip case and require normal final-tree checks after producer acceptance.
responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: Persist lease-fenced immutable start/end provenance for each blocked producer attempt, derive and review its candidates with the retry segment, and refuse ambiguous rebase provenance or silently included unrelated changes; test a pre-block test commit followed by a no-op retry.

output.summary: Preserve verified producer-attempt provenance through blocked retries so tests committed before a no-op retry remain in the reviewed scope, and refuse preserved consumer checkpoints while their producer is blocked. Recover damaged goals from accepted Git history with explicit CAS, capability-gated compatibility, and independent review.

Both independent re-reviews approve the corrected design and report no remaining candidates. The design now captures verified producer-attempt provenance and refuses consumer submission while the producer is blocked, with explicit end-to-end regressions. No notes remain.

findings.impact: A newly accepted test can remain unfrozen after the retry, allowing a later implementation to change it and leaving the independent review scope incomplete.
findings.text: The proposed union with the existing lease-to-checkpoint change set misses tests committed during a blocked attempt: blocked_record synchronizes and pushes an ahead work branch, so the next lease starts at that advanced commit. A retry that then submits without further changes sees an empty diff and never adds those newly accepted paths. Specify a provenance-safe way to identify all producer test commits since the last accepted checkpoint across blocked attempts (and rebases/syncs), and test a test commit made before a block followed by a no-op retry. Avoid broad diffs that include implementation files.

not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.
intent.serves: Developers who delegate project work to coding agents, and the agents doing it.

output.summary: The revised design preserves attributable producer-attempt segments and checks the blocked-work retry case.

findings.text: Add the approved capability-enabled real CLI/Git provenance and consumer-protection journeys: published tests across one or multiple blocked attempts then no-op retry and independent review, verified sync/rebase and refusal of unverifiable provenance, explicit candidate exclusions, and already-published consumer checkpoint refusal while blocked followed by protection and allowed non-test edits. Include capability-off compatibility and absent versus explicit empty scope where relevant.

Add the approved evidence-backed recovery coverage: reconstruct the G12 13/2 subset history and validate a read-only diagnostic with per-path provenance, preview and CAS-apply the existing edit, retry and require independent review; assert unchanged historical records and final protection. Cover done recovery, idempotence, stale bases and live leases, missing or ambiguous history, unrelated paths and old/capability-gated writers using real CLI/Git for history and atomicity boundaries.

output.summary: Four reproduced red regressions are useful, but enabled-capability provenance and evidence-backed recovery are not tested.

findings.text: Define the observable contracts needed to independently test the approved capability-enabled and recovery behavior: how a caller identifies the required capability without guessing its name, and the stable machine-readable validate diagnostic fields for per-path provenance, observed goal base and an exact edit proposal that can be applied through the existing CLI. The current design explicitly leaves the capability identifier unspecified and only describes the recovery output narratively, so tests cannot reliably enable the capability, inspect the proposal or apply it without inventing an implementation-specific API. Preserve the distinction between approved contracts and internal representation.

changed_tests.observation: Measured entire new test module; four expected failures before implementation, including two local Git and CLI journeys.

cost.summary: Pre-implementation red run; all four tests executed and exposed the intended failures.

responses.review_tests:1:1: disputed: capability-enabled testing requires the design to specify a stable capability discovery contract; the existing tests cover the capability-off and preservation cases.
responses.review_tests:1:2: disputed: recovery testing requires a specified machine-readable validate proposal, provenance and edit interface; the design does not define how those values are obtained.

spec:
Fix loss of test-path protection when a preserved test-producing node is blocked and then retried. This defect is blocking Project Base G12, which needs all accepted tests protected before implementation proceeds.

Observed reproduction: in Breeze-Block-Games/project-base G12, test_design attempt 6 at goal commit 162d60c recorded 13 frozen paths and test checkpoint ad39eb5. Attempt 7 was blocked; its record discarded the frozen field. Attempt 8 completed at goal commit b493523 with a later test checkpoint 082177c, but recorded only two frozen paths. The earlier tests remain in that checkpoint; they were not deleted. In the affected engine, frozen_paths() carries previous frozen paths only when the immediately preceding record is done, so an intervening blocked record loses the prior protection. Git preserve checks and subsequent review scope then omit those paths.

Acceptance criteria:
- A preserved test checkpoint retains all applicable previously accepted frozen test paths across blocked attempts, retries, correction rounds, and design-driven invalidation; protect later newly added test paths as well. Do not silently freeze unrelated source or submodule gitlink paths.
- Add direct regression tests that reproduce the observed done → blocked → retry/success sequence and prove later implementation modifications to every accepted frozen path are refused. Cover checkpoint ancestry and repeated blocked attempts as appropriate; preserve legitimate test corrections and existing history semantics.
- Provide a supported, validated, provenance-preserving way to recover an already affected goal, including Project Base G12: restore protection for the actual union of accepted test paths at its latest checkpoint without discarding later tests, falsifying checkpoint identity/history, waiving the review finding, or adding meaningless changes to test files. Exercise recovery and subsequent independent review in a realistic local Git/remote fixture.
- Verify compatibility and upgrade behavior for existing goals and older records, and document the recovery procedure and any engine compatibility requirements. Use local-first meaningful checks against the real engine and Git; preserve existing release and CI checks.

Do not modify Project Base goal state until the recovery mechanism is implemented and validated. Avoid unrelated workflow changes or deployment.
title: Preserve accepted test paths across blocked retries and recover affected goals
